speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you tell me your age and how long these skin lesions have been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the lesions fluid-filled vesicles that are at different stages of healing, such as some being crusted while others are still blisters? Do you notice any similar lesions on the scalp, face, or inside the mouth?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of pearly papules with central umbilication is highly characteristic of Molluscum contagiosum, especially given the daycare exposure. I do not require further testing to confirm this clinical diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
